issues.summary: greenBeanFetchAllRows_ dereferences `res.body.meta.paging` with no shape gate. orderAppClassifyResponse_ only asserts `parsed.ok === true`, so an {ok:true} body missing `meta` (or `meta.paging`) throws a TypeError that propagates out of greenBeanFetchAllRows_ -> greenBeanPull_impl_ -> withScriptLock_ -> the Tuesday 05:00 trigger, directly contradicting orderAppFetch_'s documented 'a thrown fetch ... never left to propagate into a scheduled trigger' contract. This is the identical failure class the round-3 fix hardened on the shopify side by adding shopifyValidWeekBody_ (orderapp.gs:284); the greenbean path received a page cap and a paging.returned NaN/zero guard but no shape gate, so the asymmetry is unintentional. Note the sibling reads on the SAME response are all defensively guarded -- `res.body.diagnostics || {}` (line 534) and `res.body.rows || []` (line 550) -- which makes the unguarded meta.paging read stand out as an oversight rather than a deliberate assumption. Untested: every greenbean paging mock in test_code.js (lines 5103, 5108, 5132, 5158, 5178, 5202, 5215, 5232, 5271, 5423, 5461, 5499) supplies meta.paging, so no test exercises a body without it. Fix: gate the body the way shopifyValidWeekBody_ does and return null (aborting the incomplete window, which the failcount then surfaces) instead of throwing.

docs/schema.md states "`validateIngest_` places no special restriction on writing `channel='online'` directly into `Revenue`, but no connector does so today" -- the exact inverse of the guard shipped in this same phase. Code.gs validateIngest_ now rejects every `kind:'revenue'` payload containing a row whose channel is 'online' (case-insensitive, any source), and docs/ingest-contract.md documents that rejection correctly and in bold. The schema.md line was written at step 5; the guard landed in the round-2 fix commit (5637d71) and schema.md was never updated, so the two canonical docs now contradict each other on a mechanically-enforced rule. This matters more than a typical doc nit because CLAUDE.md's docs index points connector authors at schema.md specifically ('Load when writing connectors or normalization'), so the wrong half is the half they read -- they would build an online-revenue POST path against an endpoint that rejects it. Fix: replace the sentence with a pointer to the PRD-10 exclusivity rejection.

Ambiguous response shape on the excluded-gross reconciliation signal. `excluded.byStatusTotals.gross` and `excluded.cancelled.gross` are read as objects each carrying a scalar `.gross`; if the Order app actually returns byStatusTotals as a per-status map (e.g. {PENDING:{gross:N}, PARTIALLY_PAID:{...}}), `Number(undefined) || 0` silently yields 0 and excludedGross stays 0 forever. The round-1 fix added this precisely so a weekly shrink could be reconciled, and it would fail open and silent rather than loudly. No test asserts the real API shape, and there is no log for the 'bucket present but unparseable' case (truthy object, non-numeric .gross), which is the only state that would reveal the mismatch. Cheap fix: log once when `excluded` is non-empty but weekExcluded computes to 0.

orderAppRaiseDataQualityAlert_ has no threshold or suppression: greenBeanPull raises an all-day calendar event on EVERY run while any flagged intake row sits in the window. Because the window is a rolling 3 calendar months, a single un-fixed non-numeric 06_Stock_Intake cell produces roughly 13 consecutive weekly alerts. The function's own docstring reserves it for 'RARE, ACTIONABLE' states, and the run-failure alert next to it is deliberately threshold-gated (ORDERAPP_ALERT_THRESHOLD=2) -- this one is not, so it is the alert most likely to be tuned out. Same applies to the upstream-warnings alert at line 541 (deduped per pull, but not across pulls).

The greenbean source string is a bare 'greenbean' literal in six places (orderAppRunStart_ line 601, orderAppRunSkipped_ line 624, the two orderAppRaiseDataQualityAlert_ calls lines 541/643, ingestSupplierRows line 671, the snapshot filter line 664, orderAppRunSuccess_ line 745) plus embedded in GREENBEAN_RESUM_QUEUE_PROP, while the shopify half of the same file correctly routes everything through the SHOPIFY_ORDERAPP_SOURCE constant with a comment explaining why the value matters. A typo in one occurrence silently splits the failcount/heartbeat key from the row-filter key -- the run would look healthy while the snapshot diff matched nothing. Hoist a GREENBEAN_SOURCE constant for parity.

The pre-ingest snapshot key lowercases but does not trim (`'greenbean||' + String(existingRow[3]).toLowerCase()`, and the lookup at line 685 likewise), whereas upsertRows_'s rowKey_ (Code.gs:612) does `String(v).trim().toLowerCase()`. The lowercasing was added deliberately in the round-2 fix to match rowKey_; the trim half was missed. A stored invoice_ref carrying surrounding whitespace would therefore be UPDATED in place by ingestSupplierRows but MISSED by the snapshot lookup, so a changed invoice is misclassified as new and addAffectedWeek queues the recomputed date's week instead of the stored date's week -- the exact misclassification the snapshot was built to prevent. Low likelihood today (both sides derive from the same untrimmed greenBeanInvoices_ output), but the guard is one `.trim()` and the asymmetry is a latent trap for any hand-edited Suppliers row.
